text: My name is Koh Tze Rui
Year 3 Computer Engineering student at NUS
I always knew I wanted to be an engineer.
Chasing hard problems. Chasing that intellectual high.
So I tried everything.
SWE. Containerisation. Abstraction.
Then quant — algorithm books, grinding, chasing the money. 💸
After two years of this — during national service and into uni...
I just got really bored.
By Year 1, I'd quietly stepped away from engineering. 😶
I didn't know what I was looking for.
Just knew none of it felt like enough.
Then one day, a friend sent me a link.
An HPC competition. Build a single board computer cluster.
I thought — why not?
And just like that, the lights came back on. 💡
Grinding through the night to chase the last bit of performance.
That's the kind of challenge that keeps me alive. 🔥
Sometimes you don't find your path by walking forward.
You find it by getting bored enough to look sideways.
Every dead end taught me something. Every detour shaped what I was actually looking for.
Keep chasing the problem that won't let you sleep.
I used to think engineers were the ones who built the most.
Now I think they're the ones who refuse to stop until it's right.
